facts.statement: The genus Vespersaurus was named and described in 2019.
facts.quote: One of these was named and described in 2019 as Vespersaurus.

facts.statement: Vespersaurus is a noasaurid theropod dinosaur from the Cretaceous Rio Paraná Formation in the Paraná Basin, Brazil.
facts.quote: Vespersaurus (meaning "western lizard") is a genus of noasaurid theropod dinosaur from the Cretaceous Rio Paraná Formation in the Paraná Basin, Brazil.

facts.statement: Vespersaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 90 million years ago in the Turonian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Vespersaurus paranaensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Vespersaurus de dinosaurio terópodo noasáurido que vivió a mediados del periodo Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 90 millones de años durante el Turoniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPCO.V 0065d was found in dark red sandstones of the Rio Paraná Formation in Brazil.
facts.quote: The holotype, MPCO.V 0065d, was recovered from the Late Cretaceous period, found on dark red sandstones in the Rio Paraná Formation in the Paraná Basin, Brazil.

facts.statement: The estimated body mass of Vespersaurus is 11.28 kilograms.
facts.quote: The estimated body mass of Vespersaurus is 11.28 kg

facts.statement: Vespersaurus had a functionally monodactyl foot where the large third digit bore most of the weight while walking.
facts.quote: The taxon is notable for its distinct, functionally monodactyl foot anatomy, where the singularly large third digit would have borne most of the weight while walking.

facts.statement: The genus Vespersaurus was established by Langer et al. in 2019.
facts.quote: authority: Langer et al., 2019

facts.statement: Vespersaurus belongs to the family Noasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Noasauridae

facts.statement: Vespersaurus is classified within the subfamily Noasaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Noasaurinae

facts.statement: Finite Element Analysis showed Vespersaurus teeth were not well suited for struggling or hard prey, with an ideal bite angle of 45 degrees.
facts.quote: They found that the teeth were not well suited to handle struggling prey items, nor well-equipped to handle hard food items, having an ideal bite angle of 45 degrees.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded Vespersaurus was a generalist feeder focusing on small prey rather than a top predator.
facts.quote: Based on this, the team concluded that Vespersaurus did not fill a top predator niche in the Brazilian Caiua desert where it lived, but instead filled a more generalist niche, focussing on small prey items or having an opportunistic feeding strategy.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the ichnospecies Farlowichnus rapidus was made by Vespersaurus, as some researchers question the noasaurid interpretation due to anatomical differences.
facts.quote: However, Navarro et al. (2025) questioned the noasaurid interpretation for the trackmaker of Farlowichnus due to the difference in pedal and ungual anatomy compared to those of Vespersaurus.

facts.statement: The radius of Vespersaurus is 47% the length of the humerus and ten times longer than wide, making it much thinner than most of its relatives.
facts.quote: El radio es el 47 % de la longitud del húmero y es diez veces más largo que ancho, mucho más delgado que la mayoría de sus parientes.

facts.statement: The forearm axis of Vespersaurus is twisted 25 degrees relative to the longitudinal axis.
facts.quote: El eje está torcido 25° sobre el eje longitudinal.

facts.statement: In the second finger, the penultimate phalanx is not extended, a feature exclusive to Averostra.
facts.quote: En el segundo dedo, la penúltima falange no está extendida, lo cual es exclusivo de Averostra.

facts.statement: The claw of the third finger is short, blunt, and not curved.
facts.quote: La garra de la tercera mano, un elemento corto y romo, no está curvada.

facts.statement: The second metatarsal bone is extremely flattened transversely, being less than one-fifth the width of the third metatarsal bone.
facts.quote: El segundo hueso metatarsiano está extremadamente aplanado transversalmente a menos de una quinta parte del ancho del tercer hueso metatarsiano.

facts.statement: The fourth metatarsal bone is strongly flattened, four times narrower than it is wide from front to back.
facts.quote: El cuarto hueso metatarsiano también está fuertemente aplanado, cuatro veces más estrecho que ancho de adelante hacia atrás.

facts.statement: The phalanx formula for the foot is the usual 2-3-4-5-0 found in related species.
facts.quote: La fórmula para las falanges es la habitual 2-3-4-5-0 para familiares.

facts.statement: The first phalanx of the first toe is elongated, four times longer than it is wide.
facts.quote: La primera falange del primer dedo del pie es alargada, cuatro veces más larga que ancha.

facts.statement: In 2019, Vespersaurus was placed within Abelisauroidea in the subfamily Noasaurinae as the sister species to Velocisaurus.
facts.quote: Vespersaurus se colocó dentro de Abelisauroidea en Noasaurinae en 2019, como una especie hermana de Velocisaurus, como se muestra en este cladograma.

facts.statement: The second and fourth toes of Vespersaurus were so flattened transversely that the third toe likely supported most of the animal's weight.
facts.quote: La característica más inusual de Vespersaurus es que los dedos segundo y cuarto están tan aplanados transversalmente que el tercer dedo debe haber soportado la mayor parte del peso.

facts.statement: The foot claws of Vespersaurus were not particularly curved and likely inflicted longitudinal wounds rather than piercing skin.
facts.quote: Las garras de los pies de Vespersaurus no están especialmente curvadas y es más probable que hayan infligido heridas longitudinales.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the second and fourth claws may have lifted slightly during walking to avoid hindering the push of the long third toe.
facts.quote: Quizás las garras segunda y cuarta se levantaron un poco al caminar para no entorpecer el empuje del tercer dedo largo.

facts.statement: Footprints found near the site resemble those of the ichnogenus Sarmientichnus, which some Chinese researchers believe belongs to the Deinonychosauria.
facts.quote: Se asemejan a los del Jurásico Argentino ichnogenus Sarmientichnus, que algunos investigadores chinos creen que es un miembro de la Deinonychosauria.

facts.statement: The footprints indicate an animal with a hip height of half a meter that moved quickly with hind legs at right angles.
facts.quote: Esto indica un animal con una altura de cadera de medio metro que se movía rápidamente con las patas traseras en ángulo recto entre sí.

facts.statement: A whole branch of these animals likely populated the 1.3 million square kilometer Botucatu Desert for millions of years.
facts.quote: Una rama entera de estos animales habría poblado el desierto de Botucatu de 1,3 millones de kilómetros cuadrados durante millones de años.

facts.statement: Vespersaurus lived from the Aptian to the Campanian stages, between 121.4 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Campanian (121.4 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Vespersaurus belongs to the parent group Noasaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Noasaurinae

facts.statement: Vespersaurus is classified in the family Noasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Noasauridae

facts.statement: Vespersaurus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Vespersaurus is Vespersaurus paranaensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Vespersaurus paranaensis

facts.statement: The fossil site also yielded remains of the small relative Berthasaura, whose toothless beak indicates a herbivorous lifestyle.
facts.quote: El sitio también arrojó los restos del igualmente pequeño pariente Berthasaura, cuyo pico desdentado indica una vida como herbívoro.
